Here are the genuine issues I found:

- **`queue.py`**: Mutable default argument `items=[]` causes separate `TaskQueue` instances to share the same backing list.
- **`queue.py`**: `is_full()` checks `len(self._items) > self.capacity`, so the queue accepts one element beyond its stated capacity (off-by-one).
- **`scheduler.py`**: `run_with_retry()` never increments `attempts`, causing an infinite loop whenever the worker returns `None`.
- **`store.py`**: `find_by_name()` interpolates `name` directly into the SQL query via `"%s" % name`, making it vulnerable to SQL injection.
- **`worker.py`**: `run_once()` opens the log file but never closes it, leaking file descriptors.
- **`worker.py`**: `run_once()` catches and silently discards all handler exceptions, making task failures indistinguishable from success and leaving no error record.
